facts.raw_span: stage IV B-RAF V600E mutant malignant melanoma
metastases of the liver, lungs, and peritoneum
Photodistributed erythematous to violaceous eruption
Diffuse erythema of forehead and midface, involving nasolabial folds
Erythema and edema of upper eyelids
Creatine kinase: 1088 U/L
Antinuclear antibody titer: 1:640 with speckled pattern
Jo-1 antibody: negative
MRI showed mild short TI inversion recovery hyperintensity of bilateral vastus lateralis and rectus femoris muscles
Vastus lateralis muscle biopsy showed atrophy of type II muscle fibers
Grade 4/5 strength on resisted abduction of shoulders bilaterally
Limited flexion of both hips

concepts.why: Patient presents with skin symptoms, muscle weakness, and elevated creatine kinase, which are characteristic of dermatomyositis.
Patient has a cancer diagnosis and presents with dermatomyositis-like symptoms, suggesting a paraneoplastic syndrome.
Patient has elevated inflammatory markers and autoantibodies, which are characteristic of autoimmune myopathy.
Patient presents with muscle weakness and elevated creatine kinase, which are characteristic of polymyositis.
Patient has a positive antinuclear antibody titer and presents with muscle weakness, which are characteristic of lupus myositis.
Patient presents with muscle weakness and elevated creatine kinase, which are characteristic of inclusion body myositis.
Patient has elevated inflammatory markers and autoantibodies, which are characteristic of necrotizing autoimmune myopathy.
Patient has a cancer diagnosis and presents with a multi-organ autoimmune syndrome, suggesting a paraneoplastic syndrome.
Patient presents with skin symptoms characteristic of dermatomyositis, but without significant muscle weakness.
Patient presents with skin symptoms and mildly elevated creatine kinase, characteristic of clinically amyopathic dermatomyositis.

rationales.F01: The presence of stage IV B-RAF V600E mutant malignant melanoma suggests a possible paraneoplastic syndrome, which increases the likelihood of paraneoplastic dermatomyositis.
rationales.F06: Elevated creatine kinase levels are a strong indicator of muscle damage, which is consistent with dermatomyositis, polymyositis, and necrotizing autoimmune myopathy.
rationales.F07: The presence of antinuclear antibodies with a speckled pattern is a strong indicator of lupus myositis.
rationales.F08: The absence of Jo-1 antibodies makes polymyositis and dermatomyositis less likely, but does not rule them out entirely.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's stage IV B-RAF V600E mutant malignant melanoma with metastases and the development of skin symptoms after ipilimumab treatment, along with the characteristic skin findings such as photodistributed erythematous to violaceous eruption and diffuse erythema of the forehead and midface, support the diagnosis of Paraneoplastic dermatomyositis.
